problem_restatement: The active v51 process intermittently consumes a full CPU core and has reached a 5.7 GB peak footprint because each cohort snapshot reparses complete append-only asset ledgers. Preserve exact fill, cost, markout, book, recovery, and corruption semantics while making later snapshots consume only validated appended rows.

observed_evidence.native_sample_observation: The hot sample is dominated by Python JSON scanner recursion and garbage collection while an asset ledger is open.
observed_evidence.source_trace: MultiAssetLiveRunner._finish_cycle calls MultiAssetCohortTelemetry.emit_snapshot; emit_snapshot called compatible_execution_rows for every asset; compatible_execution_rows called SolLiveLedger.read_all from byte zero.
observed_evidence.live_impact_observed: No missed order, fault, lost stop, or stale lifecycle was observed. The checkpoint remained running_consistent and SOL/SPCX retained owned venue stops.
observed_evidence.live_risk_if_unfixed: Growing ledgers can extend cycle latency or terminate the backend under memory pressure, which would leave venue stops intact but suspend timed/provider exits and new telemetry.

root_cause.cause: Snapshot telemetry repeatedly performed O(total historical asset-ledger bytes) JSON decoding instead of O(new appended bytes) consumption.
root_cause.contradictory_evidence: A second sample caught public-network waits rather than JSON decoding, so not every high-latency interval is caused by ledger parsing. The first hot sample and direct code path establish that full rescans are nevertheless real.
root_cause.falsifier: A source-level or runtime trace showing that emit_snapshot does not call full read_all for each asset would invalidate this diagnosis; the red regression observed two complete reads per asset across two snapshots.

red_results: Repeated snapshots performed two complete read_all calls per asset instead of one initialization read.
Truncating an asset ledger after the first snapshot produced a success-shaped later snapshot instead of a fail-closed error.
implementation: Add an exact byte-offset and next-sequence cursor to SolLiveLedger.
Load compatible history once and consume only rows appended by the active writer.
Reject truncation, incomplete suffixes, sequence drift, and a second writer.
Compact book history to the first post-fill markout book and latest current-run book while retaining all non-book execution evidence.

green_results.lint: Ruff passed on the scoped implementation
green_results.standards: All scoped files remain at or below 500 lines and functions at or below 50 lines

deployment_contract.reason: Restarting the active v51 process would load a broad changed worktree while SOL/SPCX are open. Venue stops remain the safer protection boundary.
deployment_contract.target: Deploy the telemetry-only remediation with v52 after the exact flat/order-free preflight and clean accounting epoch.
poststart_validation: No repeated complete asset-ledger reads after initialization.
Snapshot books, fills, costs, funding, markouts, and lifecycle attribution reconcile with the append-only ledger.
Cycle latency and process footprint remain bounded as books accumulate.
Any truncation, suffix corruption, or second writer fails closed with a durable runtime fault.

recommendation.recommendation: Include the incremental ledger projection repair in the flat-boundary v52 deployment and do not hot-restart protected v51 solely for telemetry performance.
recommendation.why_now: The active process has already reached a 5.7 GB peak footprint and repeated full rescans will worsen as append-only ledgers grow.
recommendation.evidence_reviewed: Two native process samples, repeated CPU measurements, live checkpoint health/protection, the runner-to-telemetry call path, red/green regressions, and expanded recovery/telemetry tests.
recommendation.observed_problem_or_opportunity: Remove an avoidable O(history) operation from every cycle before the two-asset v52 live run begins.
recommendation.applicable_market_regime: All regimes; this is runtime infrastructure rather than a trading signal.
recommendation.alternatives_considered: Hot-restart v51, disable snapshots, increase poll time, retain all parsed rows forever, or use an incremental validated compact projection.
recommendation.proposed_live_change: No strategy or risk change. Load the repaired telemetry implementation only at the approved flat v52 process start.
recommendation.expected_upside: Lower cycle latency and memory churn, reducing the chance that operational load delays exits or terminates backend management.
recommendation.main_risks_and_failure_modes: Cursor drift, external writer collision, lost historical markout evidence, stale latest-book projection, or compaction changing fill attribution.
recommendation.validation_completed: TDD reproduced both full rescans and success-shaped truncation; focused and expanded suites cover append, restart, truncation, torn suffix, second writer, markout, costs, books, funding, provider exits, maximum holds, and regime recovery.
recommendation.validation_still_required: Fresh v52 post-start observation of CPU, memory, cycle latency, and exact checkpoint-versus-ledger projection equivalence.
recommendation.success_metrics: One complete read per asset at initialization, only appended-row reads afterward, bounded cached books, no projection mismatch, and no stale controller cycle attributable to telemetry.
recommendation.failure_or_rollback_triggers: Any missing fill/book/cost, cursor or sequence false positive, unexplained checkpoint difference, process memory growth inconsistent with compact history, or delayed lifecycle controller.
recommendation.confidence_level: high on root cause and offline correctness; medium-high on live operational benefit until v52 post-start measurements exist
recommendation.explicit_approval_requested: Approval remains required for the flat-boundary v52 live start; this report does not arm or restart a backend.

highest_value_next_investigation.reason: After technical acceptance and telemetry latency verification, exact live route outcomes—especially HYPE short and BTC occupancy collisions—remain the largest unresolved economic evidence gap.
